interpretation: Task timing is emitted once per actual read task; joins are not separate native reads.
Revision/time alignment is used only when exactly one matching task exists; ambiguity is preserved.
A negative fresh-minus-whole-task duration can mean joining a task that was already in progress.
Native begin-before-await interval includes scheduling, hashing and process startup; it is not pure hash time.
Native end-to-return includes helper completion, IPC, decoding and scheduling; it is not pure main-actor delay.
No-overlap with fewer than two witnesses or no held choice is not an idle-gate acceptance result.
Sampler reapedMonotonic is process cleanup time, not the end of the capture window.
